species.name: Barred Long-tailed Cuckoo
species.range: patchy in lowland to submontane forest, riparian woodland, and coastal thickets, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to central Kenya, and southward to southern Mozambique, and in middle Zambezi River forest of southern Zambia and adjacent Zimbabwe; some highland breeders migrate westward

species.name: Fork-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo
species.range: Himalayan foothills, central and southern India, and Sri Lanka

species.name: Black Cuckoo
species.range: lowland and foothill forest, open woodland, riparian woodland, farmbush, and acacia thicket, from Sierra Leone eastward to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and western Kenya, and southward to northeastern Namibia and southern South Africa; southern and eastern populations migrate post-breeding to equatorial and West Africa, northward to Senegambia and eastward to southern Chad

species.name: Red-chested Cuckoo
species.range: intra-African migrant south of the Sahara

species.name: Lesser Cuckoo
species.range: breeds southern and eastern Asia; winters peninsular India, Sri Lanka, and eastern Africa

species.name: African Cuckoo
species.range: Senegambia to Somalia and South Africa

species.name: Madagascar Cuckoo
species.range: breeds Madagascar; winters in eastern Africa

species.name: Common Cuckoo
species.range: lowland to montane forest, woodland, moor, and wooded steppe, across the Palearctic from western Europe eastward to Kamchatka and Japan, and southward to northwestern Africa, northern Iran, northern India, and southern China; winters to central and southern Africa, and south Asia

species.name: Pennant-winged Nightjar
species.range: brachystegia woodland of southern Africa

species.name: Standard-winged Nightjar
species.range: in breeding season from Senegambia to Liberia, eastward to southwestern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Uganda (present during the season in southern portion of this region, but breeding there not confirmed); winters north and east from southern Mauritania and northern Sengeal eastward to central Chad, southern Sudan, eastern South Sudan, central Uganda, Eritrea, western Ethiopia, and western Kenya

species.name: Eurasian Nightjar
species.range: breeds British Isles, Iberian Peninsula, and northwestern Africa through southern Fennoscandia, Turkey, and Afghanistan to Mongolia and southern Russia; winters mainly eastern Africa

species.name: Sombre Nightjar
species.range: Ethiopia to northwestern Somalia, southwestern Kenya, and northeastern Tanzania

species.name: Rufous-cheeked Nightjar
species.range: lowland and foothill wooded savanna, miombo woodland, acacia thornscrub, and semi-desert, breeding from central Angola eastward to Zimbabwe, and southward through eastern Namibia and Botswana to southern South Africa; entire population migrates towards western equatorial Africa, wintering mostly in Cameroon and Nigeria

species.name: Egyptian Nightjar
species.range: disjunctly in lowland to foothill desert and semi-desert from Morocco to Tunisia, and in Nile Valley (Egypt), and from northern Arabian Peninsula and Iraq northeastward to central Kazakhstan and far western Pakistan; winters in the African Sahel

species.name: Nubian Nightjar
species.range: disjunctly in lowland to foothill dry and sparsely vegetated wadis, acacia thicket, desert thornscrub, and coastal dunes with scrub, in Dead Sea depression of Israel and Jordan, western Arabian Peninsula, Nile Valley from southeastern Egypt southward to central Sudan, from Eritrea and central Ethiopia eastward to northern Somalia, Socotra, and from southern Ethiopia southward to southern Kenya; Arabian population partially migratory

species.name: Golden Nightjar
species.range: lowland to foothill rocky hills, semi-desert with grass and scrub, and fallow cultivation, from southern Mauritania and northern Senegal eastward across the Sahel to central and southern Sudan; local post-breeding dispersal

species.name: Donaldson Smith's Nightjar
species.range: northwestern and southern Somalia, eastern and southern Ethiopia, eastern Kenya, and northeastern Tanzania; possibly also in southeastern South Sudan

species.name: Fiery-necked Nightjar
species.range: widely distributed in sub-Saharan Africa in lowland and foothill wooded savanna, miombo and mopane woodland, acacia scrub, and riparian thicket, from Senegambia eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward (avoiding rainforest and arid southwestern Africa) to northern Namibia and southern South Africa; some southern populations migratory northward post-breeding

species.name: Montane Nightjar
species.range: very patchy in foothill to montane forest, pine and juniper woodland, bamboo, grassland, and open scrubland, from southwestern Arabian Peninsula, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, southward through East Africa to northeastern Zambia and Malawi, and western Angola

species.name: Swamp Nightjar
species.range: very patchy in lowland and foothill wet grassland adjacent to swamps, floodplain meadows, and bogs and dambos, from Gambia and Mali eastward to South Sudan and western Ethiopia, and southward through eastern Angola to southeastern South Africa

species.name: Plain Nightjar
species.range: thornscrub of sub-Saharan Africa and southwestern Arabian Peninsula

species.name: Star-spotted Nightjar
species.range: southern South Sudan, Ethiopia (and northern Somalia?), and northern Kenya

species.name: Nechisar Nightjar
species.range: described from one wing from a road corpse found in Nechisar plains, south-central Ethiopia

species.name: Freckled Nightjar
species.range: very patchy across sub-Saharan Africa in lowland to submontane rocky terrain, kopjes and inselbergs, and wooded escarpments in miombo and mopane woodland, from southern Senegal, Mali, and Guinea eastward to Ethiopia, and southward (avoiding rainforest) to southern South Africa

species.name: Bates's Nightjar
species.range: Congo River Basin (southern Cameroon to northern Gabon, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and western Uganda)

species.name: Long-tailed Nightjar
species.range: lowland and foothill arid semi-deserts, savanna, grassland, open woodland, forest edges and clearings, and recently burned land, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward through the Sahel to eastern Sudan, Eritrea, and western Ethiopia, and southward to central Cameroon and western Uganda; northern populations migrate southward, reaching Gabon and northwestern Kenya

species.name: Slender-tailed Nightjar
species.range: southeastern South Sudan, Ethiopia, Djibouti, northwestern and southern Somalia, Uganda, Kenya, and northeastern Tanzania

species.name: Square-tailed Nightjar
species.range: lowland and foothill wooded grassland, savanna, miombo and mopane woodland, and thornbush country, from western Gabon eastward to eastern Tanzania, including Pemba and Unguja (in Zanzibar), and southward to northern Namibia and eastern South Africa and Eswatini; non-breeding visitor northward to northern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southern Kenya

species.name: Mottled Spinetail
species.range: patchy in lowland and foothill dry deciduous woodland with baobabs, and savanna with fan palms, from Senegambia eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southeastern Kenya, southward to western Angola, and through Tanzania including Pemba and Unguja (in Zanzibar) to eastern Zimbabwe and northeastern South Africa

species.name: Sabine's Spinetail
species.range: rainforest of southern Guinea to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, western Uganda, and western Kenya

species.name: Cassin's Spinetail
species.range: Sierra Leone and Liberia to northwestern Angola and western Uganda; Bioko

species.name: Bat-like Spinetail
species.range: disjunctly in lowland and foothill wooded savanna, miombo woodland, and open woodland with baobabs, of western Angola, and from southeastern Kenya, Tanzania, and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to eastern Zimbabwe and far northeastern South Africa

species.name: Scarce Swift
species.range: patchy in foothill and montane gorges and waterfalls in forest from western Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to Ethiopia and Kenya, and southward to Angola, eastern Zimbabwe, and adjacent Mozambique; post-breeding dispersal likely but poorly understood

species.name: Alpine Swift
species.range: patchy in foothill to montane habitats, wide-ranging from forest to semi-desert steppe, from Iberia and Morocco eastward across southern Europe, the Middle East, and the Himalayas, to southern Kazakhstan and northeastern India, and southward to southern Africa, Madagascar, the Arabian Peninsula, southwestern India, and Sri Lanka; migratory populations winter to the African tropics and to central India

species.name: Mottled Swift
species.range: very patchy in foothill and montane granite highlands in Sierra Leone, Mali, Ghana, Nigeria, western Sudan, and northern Angola, and from Eritrea and Ethiopia southward through East Africa to Zimbabwe and central Mozambique; widespread post-breeding dispersal and nomadic wandering

species.name: Common Swift
species.range: lowland to montane habitats, wide-ranging from woodland to semi-desert steppe, from western Europe eastward to central Siberia, and southward to northwestern Africa, Iran, northwestern India, and central China; long-distance migrant to central and southern Africa

species.name: Nyanza Swift
species.range: disjunctly in lowland to montane cliffs and gorges in mostly arid highlands of Eritrea, Ethiopia, and northern Somalia, and northeastern Uganda, western Kenya, and northern Tanzania; Somali population migratory, mostly westward and southward

species.name: Pallid Swift
species.range: patchy in lowland to montane forest, sea-cliffs and gorges, and urban areas, from Iberia eastward to southern Iran, and southward to western Mauritania, locally in the Sahara, and Egypt and Arabian Peninsula; northern populations winter to the African Sahel, and coastal Pakistan

species.name: African Swift
species.range: foothill and montane cliffs from Sierra Leone eastward through Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to northern Kenya, and southward to Angola and South Africa; some populations are intra-African migrants

species.name: Forbes-Watson's Swift
species.range: breeds southern Arabia (southern Yemen and southwest Oman) and coastal Somalia, and resident Socotra; winters to coastal Kenya

species.name: Little Swift
species.range: Africa including Gulf of Guinea islands eastward to sub-Himalayan India, southward to southern India and Sri Lanka

species.name: Horus Swift
species.range: Nigeria and Cameroon eastward to Ethiopia and southward to western angola and southern South Africa

species.name: White-rumped Swift
species.range: southern Iberian Peninsula, central Morocco, and sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: African Palm Swift
species.range: widespread sub-Saharan Africa in lowland and foothill habitats with palms, especially fan and lala palms, from Senegambia eastward through Nigeria, and Gulf of Guinea islands, to Ethiopia, Eritrea, and southwestern Arabian Peninsula, and southward to South Africa; some populations exhibit post-breeding dispersal

species.name: White-spotted Flufftail
species.range: lowland to foothill rainforest, forest swamps and pools, and dense thicket in gallery forest, from Senegambia eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

species.name: Buff-spotted Flufftail
species.range: patchy in lowland to montane thicket, scrub, and forest, including juniper and bamboo, from Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward through Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to southwestern Ethiopia and southwestern Kenya, and southward to southern Angola and southern South Africa

species.name: Red-chested Flufftail
species.range: very patchy in sub-Saharan Africa in lowland to montane wetland habitat, including wet grassland, sedge meadow, and papyrus swamps, from Sierra Leone eastward to western Ethiopia, and southward through Angola and Tanzania, including Pemba and Unguja (in Zanzibar), to southern South Africa

species.name: Chestnut-headed Flufftail
species.range: very patchy in lowland and foothill grassy marsh in savanna or forest, lakeside marsh, and dambos, from Cameroon and Gabon eastward to Rwanda (and long ago, Tanzania), and southward to central Angola and central Malawi

species.name: Streaky-breasted Flufftail
species.range: locally in wet grassland of central Africa

species.name: Striped Flufftail
species.range: disjunctly in lowland to montane dry upland grassland, bracken bramble, and lowland Fynbos, from southern South Sudan and southwestern Kenya southward to Malawi, eastern Zimbabwe, and adjacent Mozambique, and Eswatini and eastern and southern South Africa

species.name: White-winged Flufftail
species.range: highlands of Ethiopia and eastern South Africa

species.name: Water Rail
species.range: lowland to foothill reedbeds, marsh, and swamps, from Europe eastward to central Russia, and southward to northwestern Africa, Iran, northwestern India, and western China; northern populations winter to Nile River valley (Egypt), Arabian Peninsula, and western India

species.name: African Rail
species.range: swamps and reedbeds of eastern and southern Africa

species.name: Corn Crake
species.range: breeds British Isles eastward to northwestern China and central Siberia, and southward from central Europe, the Caucasus, Kyrgyzstan, northwestern Xinjiang (northwestern China), and northern Mongolia; winters mainly from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southern Tanzania southward to eastern South Africa

species.name: African Crake
species.range: sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal eastward to Kenya and southward to northern and eastern South Africa, except in driest areas

species.name: Rouget's Rail
species.range: highlands of Eritrea and Ethiopia

species.name: Gray-throated Rail
species.range: rainforest of Sierra Leone to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda

species.name: Spotted Crake
species.range: breeds British Isles (very locally) and Spain eastward across southern Scandinavia and northern Mediterranean to western and central Russia, Arabia, and northwestern Mongolia; winters Mediterranean to southern Africa and southeastern Asia

species.name: Lesser Moorhen
species.range: aquatic habitats from Senegambia eastward to central Ethiopia, southward to central Namibia and east-central South Africa

species.name: Eurasian Moorhen
species.range: breeds Europe, Africa, Malagasy region, and Macaronesian islands eastward through Asia to Japan, the Philippines, and Mariana Islands, and southward to Sri Lanka and central Malayan Peninsula; winters to Arabia and southern China

species.name: Eurasian Coot
species.range: breeds Europe, northern Africa, Azores and Canaries eastward through central Asia to Japan and southward to Indian Subcontinent, including Sri Lanka, Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia, and New Zealand; winters to Africa, Indonesia, and Philippines

species.name: Red-knobbed Coot
species.range: southern Spain and Morocco; eastern and southern Africa and Madagascar

species.name: Allen's Gallinule
species.range: sub-Saharan Africa, Madagascar, and Comoros

species.name: African Swamphen
species.range: Egypt, sub-Saharan Africa, and Madagascar

species.name: Nkulengu Rail
species.range: humid forest of Sierra Leone to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Gabon

species.name: Striped Crake
species.range: locally in sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Black Crake
species.range: sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Little Crake
species.range: breeds locally in Europe eastward to western Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, and western Xinjiang; winters Mediterranean to Africa and India

species.name: Baillon's Crake
species.range: widespread but patchy in Old World in lowland to submontane marsh, wet meadow, peat bog, and salt-marsh, from Iberia and southern Europe eastward through the Middle East and northern India to southern Siberia, Mongolia, and Japan, and southward to eastern and southern Africa, Madagascar, Sumatra, Borneo, New Guinea, Australia, and New Zealand; northern populations migratory to the tropics, with western Palearctic populations wintering in Africa and eastern Palearctic populations wintering to India and Indonesia

species.name: African Finfoot
species.range: lowland to submontane silt-free, well-vegetated rivers and lakes in forest and woodland, and mangroves, from Senegambia eastward to western Ethiopia and southeastern Kenya, and southward to southern Angola, northeastern Namibia, and southern South Africa

species.name: Gray Crowned-Crane
species.range: lowland and foothill shallow wetland, marsh, grassland, and savanna, from central Uganda and central Kenya southward through East Africa to southern Angola and northern Namibia to central Mozambique, and disjunctly in eastern and southern South Africa; some seasonal dispersal

species.name: Black Crowned-Crane
species.range: patchy in lowland and foothill shallow wetland and grassland from Senegambia and southern Mauritania eastward in the Sahel to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and western Ethiopia, southward to South Sudan and far northern Kenya; some seasonal dispersal

species.name: Wattled Crane
species.range: patchily distributed northeastern and southern Africa

species.name: Demoiselle Crane
species.range: breeds Palearctic; winters in northeastern Africa and southern Asia

species.name: Common Crane
species.range: breeds northern Eurasia; winters to northern Africa, southern India, and southeastern Asia

species.name: Spotted Thick-knee
species.range: lowland to montane arid open woodland, savanna, lightly wooded grassland, and stony slopes and beaches, from Senegal eastward through the Sahel to Eritrea, Somalia, and southern Arabian Peninsula, and southward through East Africa and Angola eastward to Mozambique and southern South Africa; some dry season wandering

species.name: Water Thick-knee
species.range: wetland edges near woodland from Liberia eastward to southern Somalia and southward to southernmost South Africa

species.name: Eurasian Thick-knee
species.range: breeds open flat areas near sparse cover from England eastward to northeastern Xinjiang (western China), in south from Mauretania eastward to western and central Pakistan, and including Canary Islands (central Macaronesia) and some Mediterranean islands; winters to south as far as southern Kenya and Arabian Peninsula

species.name: Senegal Thick-knee
species.range: sandy lake and river banks from Senegal eastward to Ethiopia and southward to Cameroon and Kenya; also Egypt and Sudan

species.name: Egyptian Plover
species.range: Senegal and Gambia eastward to Ethiopia, southward to far northern Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Sudan; formerly also Nile River, Egypt

species.name: Black-winged Stilt
species.range: breeds from southern Europe, and Cape Verde Islands, northern and sub-Saharan Africa, Socotra, and coastal Madagascar eastward to southeastern Russia, eastern China, south-central Japan, Taiwan, east-central Philippines, southward to northern Middle East, Sri Lanka, Malayan Peninsula, eastward to western Java; winters to Greater Sundas and Philippines

species.name: Pied Avocet
species.range: breeds locally southern and central Europe eastward to northeastern Russia and China southward through Middle East to northwestern India; also eastern and southern Africa; winters to coastal northern Africa, inland western Africa, Indian Peninsula including Sri Lanka, and to eastern China

species.name: Eurasian Oystercatcher
species.range: breeds coastally and inland from Iceland eastward to Kamchatka and southward to southern Europe and central and northeastern Asia; winters to coasts of tropical Africa, southern Asia, and eastern China

species.name: African Oystercatcher
species.range: coasts of southern Africa (northern Namibia to eastern Cape Province)

species.name: Black-bellied Plover
species.range: Holarctic; almost cosmopolitan post-breeding dispersal

species.name: European Golden-Plover
species.range: breeds inland low Arctic (mainly) to temperate zone from Greenland eastward to Taymyr Peninsula (north-central Russia); winters to inland and coastal southern Europe, northern Africa, and Middle East

species.name: Pacific Golden-Plover
species.range: breeds Arctic and subarctic Russia from Yamal Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and northern Kamchatka and Bering Sea coasts of western Alaska; winters to coastal Horn of Africa and Indian subcontinent eastward through Taiwan and Indonesian Archipelago throughout Australasia and Micronesia to eastern Polynesia; widely vagrant elsewhere

species.name: Eurasian Dotterel
species.range: breeds high Arctic coastal tundra and alpine zone, from northern British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and western Alaska; in south locally from Pyrenees through montane Mongolia; winters from Iberian Peninsula and northern Africa eastward to Arabian Peninsula and Iraq

species.name: Common Ringed Plover
species.range: breeds inland high Arctic Palearctic from Greenland to northeastern Siberia, in south to temperate northwestern Europe; winters to southern Europe and Mediterranean, Azores to Cape Verde Islands (Macaronesia), sub-Saharan Africa and Malagasy region eastward to Persian Gulf region

species.name: Forbes's Plover
species.range: grassland and rocky hillsides of western and central Africa

species.name: Three-banded Plover
species.range: inland northeastern to southern Africa from Nigeria in west and Egypt in the east southward through the Cape region; Madagascar

species.name: Little Ringed Plover
species.range: breeds inland subarctic to tropical zones of Eurasia east through Japan and southward through southern Asia, Philippines, New Guinea, and Bismarck Archipelago; winters sub-Saharan west-central to eastern Africa through Indonesian Archipelago

species.name: Northern Lapwing
species.range: breeds inland temperate and subarctic Eurasia from Scandinavia and Iberian Peninsula eastward to southeastern Russia and northeastern China; winters northern Africa eastward to Japan, Taiwan, and northern Vietnam

species.name: Long-toed Lapwing
species.range: inland sub-Saharan Africa, mostly from South Sudan and Kenya southward through northern Botswana and central Mozambique

species.name: Blacksmith Lapwing
species.range: inland west-central Angola to south-central Kenya and southward to South Africa

species.name: Spur-winged Lapwing
species.range: Senegambia to Red Sea, northeastern Tanzania, and eastern Mediterranean

species.name: Black-headed Lapwing
species.range: inland Sahel zone from southern Mauritania eastward to Eritrea and in south from northern Guinea eastward to far northern Tanzania

species.name: White-crowned Lapwing
species.range: sandy riverbanks of sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Senegal Lapwing
species.range: savanna of sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Black-winged Lapwing
species.range: inland northeastern to southeastern Africa from Eritrea to northern Tanzania and disjunctly eastern South Africa

species.name: Crowned Lapwing
species.range: inland northeastern to southern Africa, from northern Somalia in the northeast and Angola in the south, southward through South Africa

species.name: Wattled Lapwing
species.range: inland sub-Saharan Africa (except Congolian forest and northwestern and southwestern arid regions) from southern Mauritania east through Eritrea and southward through northeastern South Africa

species.name: Spot-breasted Lapwing
species.range: montane grassland of north-central to south-central Ethiopia

species.name: Brown-chested Lapwing
species.range: range poorly known; breeds from Nigeria east (probably) to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; disperses west to Ghana, southward to Cameroon and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and eastward to western Tanzania

species.name: Sociable Lapwing
species.range: breeds inland northern Kazakhstan and adjacent southern Russia (formerly Ukraine to Xinjiang); winters Sudan to Eritrea, Israel, Arabian Peninsula, central Pakistan, and northwestern India (now rare globally)

species.name: White-tailed Lapwing
species.range: breeds inland central Türkiye eastward to northwestern Afghanistan and southward from Persian Gulf to southwestern Pakistan; winters to Eritrea and Persian Gulf regions eastward to southwestern Pakistan

species.name: Caspian Plover
species.range: breeds central Asia from southwestern Russia and Turkmenistan eastward to northwestern Xinjiang; winters inland Kenya to south-central Africa

species.name: Siberian Sand-Plover
species.range: breeds inland and coastal eastern Russia; winters from southern coastal Japan, coastal Taiwan, and Vietnam through Indonesia to Australia, New Guinea region, Melanesia, and western Micronesia

species.name: Tibetan Sand-Plover
species.range: breeds inland central Asia and Tibetan Plateau; winters to coasts of Middle East, eastern Africa, Indian Ocean islands, and Indian subcontinent to coastal southern China, southeastern Asia, and Greater Sundas (at least)

species.name: Greater Sand-Plover
species.range: breeds inland western to east-central Asia from Turkey to eastern Mongolia; winters to coastal Middle East, eastern and southern Africa, eastward through southern Asian coasts to southern Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), Australia, Melanesia, and western Micronesia

species.name: Kittlitz's Plover
species.range: sub-Saharan Africa, northeastern Egypt, and Madagascar

species.name: Chestnut-banded Plover
species.range: inland and coastal eastern Africa in southern Kenya and northern Tanzania, and widely scattered localities in southern Africa from southern Angola and central Mozambique southward through South Africa

species.name: White-fronted Plover
species.range: coastal and inland sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal eastward to Somalia and southward through South Africa; also Madagascar and satellite islands

species.name: Kentish Plover
species.range: coastal and inland southern Palearctic from southern Europe eastward to northeastern Asia, in south through northern Africa east through Middle East and Sri Lanka to Taiwan; winters to Sahel of west-central to east-central Africa through eastern China, Indonesian Archipelago, and Philippines

species.name: Greater Painted-Snipe
species.range: locally in inland Africa, Madagascar, and Oriental region from Indus Valley (central Pakistan) to Japan, Philippines, and eastern Lesser Sundas

species.name: Lesser Jacana
species.range: lakes, ponds, and marshes of sub-Saharan Africa from Mali eastward to Ethiopia and southward to Namibia and southeastern Africa

species.name: African Jacana
species.range: lakes, ponds, and marshes of sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Eurasian Whimbrel
species.range: breeds patchily northern Palearctic and steppes of southwestern Russia; winters widely on coasts of Old World

species.name: Slender-billed Curlew
species.range: formerly bred southwestern Siberia; wintered to coastal Tunisia and Morocco; probably extinct, last verified report 2001

species.name: Eurasian Curlew
species.range: subarctic and temperate Palearctic wetlands and meadows from Faroe and British isles and Scandinavia southward to southern France, east through northern Kazakhstan and (locally) northern Mongolia to Transbaikalia (northeastern Russia), Inner Mongolia, and Heilongjiang (northeastern China); winters mainly subtropical to tropical coasts and larger rivers from Iceland, southern British Isles, southern Europe, Mediterranean, Africa, and Malagasy region through Middle East, Indian subcontinent, southeastern Asia, southern Japan, Korean Peninsula, southeastern China, Taiwan, Philippines, and Indonesian Archipelago

species.name: Bar-tailed Godwit
species.range: breeds patchily in low Arctic tundra of northern Palearctic from far northern Scandinavia to Chukotskiy and Anadyr peninsulas (northeastern Russia) and northern and western Alaska; winters mainly temperate to tropical coasts from British Isles, southern Europe, western Mediterranean, Africa, and Malagasy region through Middle East, Indian subcontinent, southeastern Asia, Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), southeastern China, Taiwan, Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, Australasia from New Guinea region to Melanesia and New Zealand, and Fiji (southwestern Polynesia)

species.name: Black-tailed Godwit
species.range: breeds in subarctic and temperate wet grassland from Iceland, Faroe and British isles, and Scandinavia southward to southwestern France, east through northwestern Russia, northern Kazakhstan, and northern Mongolia eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula, Kamchatka, Sakhalin, and Amurland (eastern Russia) and Inner Mongolia (northeastern China); winters coastal and inland temperate to tropical wetlands from southern British Isles, southern Europe, Africa (except southern), Middle East, southern Asia, Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), Taiwan, southeastern China, Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, southern New Guinea, and Australia

species.name: Asian Dowitcher
species.range: breeds inland wetlands from southwestern Siberia and eastern Kazakhstan, (probably) northern Mongolia to southeastern Siberia, and northeastern China; winters coastal southern Thailand, Malayan Peninsula, Indonesian Archipelago, and northern Australia

species.name: Jack Snipe
species.range: breeds taiga wetlands from Scandinavia and northeastern Poland to east-central Siberia; winters inland wetlands from Faroe and British islands, western and southern Europe, Mediterranean, tropical Africa, Middle East, and southern Asia

species.name: Great Snipe
species.range: breeds meadows from northern Scandinavia and eastern Poland eastward to Yenisei River (western Siberia); winters wet grassland of tropical and subtropical sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Pin-tailed Snipe
species.range: breeds low Arctic tundra to temperate montane meadows from northwestern Siberia and northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Sea of Okhotsk (eastern Siberia); winters inland wetlands from southern Arabian Peninsula eastward through southern Asia to Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan) and southward to Taiwan and Greater Sundas

species.name: African Snipe
species.range: subtropical to tropical wetlands of Africa from Eritrea southward through eastern Africa and Angola southward through South Africa

species.name: Common Snipe
species.range: breeds low Arctic to temperate wetlands of Palearctic from Iceland to British Isles, Scandinavia, France, and Azores (northern Macaronesia) east through northern Russia to central Chukotskiy Peninsula, Kamchatka, Sea of Okhotsk, and Commander Islands (southeastern Russia); in south to northern Kazakhstan, eastern Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Afghanistan, Kashmir (northwestern Himalayas), northern Mongolia, and northeastern China; winters temperate to tropical wetlands mainly north of Equator from British Isles to southern Europe, Macaronesia, northern Africa, west-central to east-central Africa, Middle East, central to southern Asia, eastern China, Taiwan, Korean Peninsula, central and southern Japan, Philippines, and Greater Sundas

species.name: Red Phalarope
species.range: breeds mostly high Arctic marshy tundra from southern Greenland and Iceland eastward across Siberia to northern Alaska and northern Canada including southern tier of Arctic Canadian islands; winters off coasts from California to southern Chile, Atlantic USA to northern Florida, and off western Africa

species.name: Red-necked Phalarope
species.range: breeds mostly low Arctic tundra from southern Greenland and Iceland eastward to Kamchatka, Kuril, and Commander islands, and Aleutians through Canada; winters off coasts of Indian Ocean from Arabian Sea eastward through Indonesian Archipelago and in Pacific to New Guinea and Bismarck Archipelago and western Mexico to Peru and Galapagos

species.name: Terek Sandpiper
species.range: breeds low Arctic tundra and taiga from Finland and Ukraine eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and southward to western Amurland (eastern Russia); winters mainly coastal mudflats and estuaries from eastern Africa eastward to Taiwan and northern Australia

species.name: Common Sandpiper
species.range: breeds inland waterbody margins from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Russia), in south from Iberian Peninsula across Caucasus to Kashmir (northwestern Himalayas), northeastern China, and Japan; winters from southwestern Europe and Africa eastward to Melanesia and Micronesia

species.name: Spotted Sandpiper
species.range: breeds inland waterbody margins from Aleutian Islands and Alaska mainland except North Slope eastward through Canada (except far northern) to Newfoundland, and southward to southwestern and east-central USA; winters southern USA and Caribbean southward to northern Chile and Argentina

species.name: Green Sandpiper
species.range: breeds taiga wetlands from Scandinavia and Germany eastward to Sakha Republic (northeastern Siberia), southward through central Asia and northeastern China; winters wetlands from British Isles southward through Africa and eastward to Japan through Philippines

species.name: Solitary Sandpiper
species.range: breeds subarctic to temperate zone taiga muskeg from Alaska mainland (except far north) to southwestern Canada, eastward to Hudson and James bays and north of Great Lakes to eastern Quebec (at least); winters inland subtropical to tropical small wetlands from west-central Mexico, southern Texas, and the Caribbean to central Peru and north-central Argentina

species.name: Marsh Sandpiper
species.range: breeds freshwater marshes from eastern Poland and Baltic states eastward through southern Russia and northern Kazakhstan to Amurland and northeastern China; winters wetlands from Africa eastward through southern Asia to southern Japan and Mariana Islands, and southward to Australia

species.name: Wood Sandpiper
species.range: breeds wooded wetlands from Scotland and Scandinavia eastward through inland northern Russia to eastern Siberia and northeastern China, in south through northern Mongolia to Commander Islands (southeastern Russia); winters small wetlands from Africa eastward to southern Japan and southward to Australia

species.name: Common Redshank
species.range: breeds subarctic to temperate coastal and inland marshes and meadows from Iceland to northern Scandinavia and southward to Iberian Peninsula and coastal Tunisia, in north from Baltics, southwestern Russia, Kazakhstan, and northern Mongolia eastward to Amurland (southeastern Russia), southward through northern Middle East, most of central Asia, Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau, and eastward to northeastern China; winters temperate to tropical inland and coastal wetlands from southern British Isles, Africa (except southern), Middle East, southern Asia to eastern China, Philippines, Taiwan, and Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), and Indonesian Archipelago

species.name: Lesser Yellowlegs
species.range: breeds subarctic tundra to forest from Alaska mainland eastward to James Bay and probably central Quebec (east-central Canada); winters southern USA throughout Caribbean southward to Tierra del Fuego

species.name: Spotted Redshank
species.range: breeds wooded tundra from Scandinavia eastward through inland Russia to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia); winters wetlands from southern British Isles and tropical Africa eastward through southern Asia to southeastern China and Taiwan

species.name: Common Greenshank
species.range: breeds taiga wetlands from Scotland and Scandinavia eastward through temperate Russia to far eastern Russia; winters from southern Europe and Africa eastward through southern Asia to central Japan and southward to Australia and western Micronesia

species.name: Ruddy Turnstone
species.range: breeds high and low Arctic tundra of coastal Holarctic; winters temperate to tropical coasts worldwide, including oceanic islands

species.name: Great Knot
species.range: breeds montane tundra of northeastern Siberia from Yakutsk eastward to Anadyr Peninsula; winters coasts from northeastern Arabian Peninsula eastward to Taiwan, Phillipines, and Australia

species.name: Red Knot
species.range: breeds patchily in high Arctic (mainly) tundra of Holarctic from northwestern and eastern Greenland, north-central Siberia, islands north of north-central and northeastern Siberia, and northern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia); winters coasts worldwide from temperate zone to tropics; in Indian Ocean mainly western Australia, and in Pacific in New Zealand but rare on other remote islands

species.name: Ruff
species.range: breeds tundra and steppe of northwestern Europe from Scandinavia southward to northern Ukraine and eastward to far eastern Siberia; winters from central Europe southward through Africa, eastward through southern Asia to central Japan southward to Philippines

species.name: Broad-billed Sandpiper
species.range: breeds patchily in low Arctic to subarctic tundra bogs of northern Palearctic from Scandinavia to Kanin Peninsula (northwestern Russia); Taimyr Peninsula (northwestern Siberia) and Lena to Kolyma rivers (northeastern Siberia); winters Paleotropical coasts from eastern Africa, Red Sea, and Persian Gulf through southeastern Asia, Indonesian Archipelago, southern New Guinea, and Australia (except south and Tasmania)

species.name: Sharp-tailed Sandpiper
species.range: breeds low Arctic tundra from Lena to Kolyma rivers (northeastern Siberia); winters from Wallacea eastward through Australasia; prone to extreme vagrancy

species.name: Curlew Sandpiper
species.range: breeds drier tundra from Yamal Peninsula to northwestern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northwestern to northeastern Siberia), including New Siberian Islands; winters southern Europe and Africa eastward through southern Asia to Taiwan and Philippines and southward to Melanesia; prone to extreme vagrancy

species.name: Temminck's Stint
species.range: breeds tundra of Scandinavia eastward through northern Russia to Chukotskiy Peninsula (notheastern Russia), including New Siberian Islands; winters southeastern Europe southward to central Africa and eastward to southern Japan and Taiwan

species.name: Long-toed Stint
species.range: breeds subarctic to temperate bogs of disjunctly in Chukotskiy Peninsula, northern Kuril and Commander islands (eastern Russia) and (perhaps) northern Mongolia; winters eastern India and Sri Lanka eastward through southern Asia to southern Japan and southward to southeastern Australia

species.name: Red-necked Stint
species.range: breeds coastal tundra of Taymyr Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and northern Kamchatka Peninsula (north-central to north-eastern Siberia); breeds coastal northeastern India and Sri Lanka eastward to Philippines, Australasia, and Melanesia

species.name: Buff-breasted Sandpiper
species.range: breeds high Arctic dry coastal tundra from Wrangel Island (northeastern Siberia) eastward through Alaskan North Slope to northeastern Canada, including Arctic islands from Banks to Devon; migrates to grassland of southeastern Brazil and Uruguay to central Argentina; prone to extreme vagrancy worldwide

species.name: Sanderling
species.range: breeds high Arctic tundra wetlands of Holarctic from northwestern and southeastern Greenland, Svalbard (north of Norway), north Taymyr Peninsula and Severnaya Zemlya (to the north), Lena Delta, and New Siberian Islands (north-central Siberia), Alaskan North Slope (rare), Canadian Arctic islands from Banks to Ellesmere and south to Southampton; winters sandy coastal beaches worldwide from temperate to tropical zone, in Old World from the British Isles and Macaronesia (northwest of northern Africa) through Africa, Malagasy region, Middle East, southern Asia through Indonesian Archipelago to Australia, Melanesia, Philippines, and south and central Japan (but rare New Guinea and New Zealand); in New World, southwestern and southeastern Canada and Caribbean south to Tierra del Fuego, and including remote islands of eastern Polynesia

species.name: Dunlin
species.range: breeds low (locally high) Arctic to temperate wet tundra of Holarctic, from southwestern and northeastern Greenland, Iceland, Faroe Islands, northern British Isles, Scandinavia, Baltic region east through northern Russia including Novaya Zemlya (north of northwestern Siberia) and New Siberian Islands (north of east-central Russia), through Chukotskiy Peninsula, western Kamchatka, northern Kurile and northern Sakhalin islands (eastern Russia); Aleutian Islands, western and northern Alaska and northwestern Canada, and north-central Canada north and west of Hudson Bay; winters coastal and inland wetlands from temperate to tropical zones mainly north of Equator, from British Isles, western Europe, Mediterranean, northern and north-central Africa, Middle East, northern Indian subcontinent to northern Vietnam and eastern China, Taiwan, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (except northern); southwestern Canada and New England to west-central Mexico and Yucatan Peninsula

species.name: Little Stint
species.range: breeds drier tundra from northern Scandinavia eastward through northern Russia to New Siberian Islands (east-central Siberia); winters mudflats and marshes from southern Europe and Africa eastward to southern Asia

species.name: White-rumped Sandpiper
species.range: breeds wet tundra from North Slope of Alaska eastward in coastal northern Canada to northwestern Hudson Bay, and Banks to Devon and Baffin islands (northeastern Canada); winters to wetlands of southern Chile, southeastern Brazil, northwestern to southeastern Argentina, and Falkland Islands

species.name: Pectoral Sandpiper
species.range: breeds wet tundra from Yamal Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northwestern to eastern Siberia), including New Siberian and Wrangel islands, also western and northern Alaska eastward through northeastern Canada, including Arctic islands; winters wet grassland and wetland edge mainly to Peru, Bolivia, and southern Brazil southward to Tierra del Fuego; prone to extreme vagrancy

species.name: Small Buttonquail
species.range: dry scrub, savanna, and burnt areas in lowlands to mountains from far southern Iberian Peninsula (at least formerly) and northern Morocco; most of sub-Saharan Africa; southwestern Arabian Peninsula; northern and southeastern Pakistan east through eastern China, southward through India and east through Vietnam; Philippines (where rare), and disjunctly Java and Bali

species.name: Black-rumped Buttonquail
species.range: Ghana to Kenya, Uganda, and southeastern Cape Province

species.name: Quail-plover
species.range: discontinuously distributed Sahel of sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Crab-Plover
species.range: breeds sandy coasts and islands of Red Sea, Arabian Peninsula and Persian Gulf; ranges southwestern Indian Ocean coast to KwaZulu Natal, Malagasy region including Seychelles, northern Indian Ocean islands eastward to western India, Sri Lanka, and Andaman Islands

species.name: Double-banded Courser
species.range: tropical to subtropical stony plains of eastern and southern Africa, disjunctly in Djibouti, Ethiopia, and northern Somalia; southern Kenya and Tanzania; and southwestern Angola to southwestern Zimbabwe and through South Africa

species.name: Bronze-winged Courser
species.range: open woodland of sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Three-banded Courser
species.range: tropical bushland and open woodland from Ethiopia and Somalia through eastern Africa to northern South Africa and west to northern Namibia

species.name: Temminck's Courser
species.range: tropical to subtropical savanna of sub-Saharan Africa from southern Mauritania eastward to Eritrea and western Somalia, southward to northern South Africa

species.name: Cream-colored Courser
species.range: subtropical to tropical desert of western Paleotropics, from eastern Canary and Cape Verde islands (central and southern Macaronesia), northwestern Africa, Middle East from southeastern Turkey to Socotra, Iran, and western Turkmenistan to far northwestern India

species.name: Somali Courser
species.range: semidesert in lowlands to hills from Eritrea and eastern Ethiopia throughout Somalia, southward to far southeastern South Sudan and east through southeastern Kenya; some intratropical migration

species.name: Rock Pratincole
species.range: rocky rivers of tropical Africa from southeastern Gambia and Guinea-Bissau, disjunctly eastward to South Sudan and Ethiopia, eastward to western Kenya and southward to northern Namibia and Mozambique

species.name: Gray Pratincole
species.range: rivers of Mali to Cameroon, western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Angola

species.name: Madagascar Pratincole
species.range: breeds rocky coastal and river islets of northwestern and eastern Madagascar; winters coasts and estuaries of eastern Africa from southern Somalia to northern Mozambique

species.name: Collared Pratincole
species.range: patchily southern temperate to tropical grassland near water, from southern Europe and northern Africa through central Asia eastward to western Xinjiang (northwestern China) and northwestern India; also sub-Saharan river systems except far south

species.name: Black-winged Pratincole
species.range: breeds saline steppe near water from central Ukraine and southwestern Russia eastward to eastern Kazakhstan; winters in grassland near water of eastern Namibia, Botswana, and northern South Africa

species.name: Long-tailed Jaeger
species.range: breeds Holarctic high and low Arctic tundra, locally in subarctic, from northwestern and southeastern Greenland, Arctic northern Scandinavia to northeastern Siberia and Kamchatka (eastern Russia); Arctic, western, and southern Alaska through Arctic Canada to Ellesmere and Baffin islands; in winter highly pelagic and mostly occurs southerly, to offshore subantarctic and subtropical waters off Africa, Madagascar, southern Australia, Peru, Chile, and east-central Argentina

species.name: Parasitic Jaeger
species.range: breeds mostly low Arctic tundra from Greenland, Iceland, and Scotland eastward to northeastern Siberia and Kamchatka, Aleutian and Bering Sea islands, through Alaska to east-central Arctic Canada (except northern high Arctic islands); winters to coastal waters of Africa, Persian Gulf, western India and Sri Lanka, eastward to Australasia, and Peru, Chile, and east-central Argentina

species.name: Pomarine Jaeger
species.range: breeds high Arctic tundra, mainly northwestern to northeastern Russia (including many high Arctic islands), northern and southwestern Alaska, eastward through Arctic Canada to Baffin Island (northeastern Canada); winters to temperate to tropical coasts and offshore waters worldwide

species.name: Great Skua
species.range: breeds Iceland, Faroe Islands, Ireland, Scotland, Norway including Svalbard, and northwestern Russia to Novaya Zemlya; winters North Atlantic Ocean offshore waters to central Gulf Stream of New England to North Carolina, northeastern Brazil, North Sea to Iberian Peninsula, western Mediterranean, Macaronesia, and western Africa

species.name: Brown Skua
species.range: southern oceans and coasts from coastal southern Argentina, Falkland Islands, Tristan da Cunha group (south-central South Atlantic), subantarctic and Antarctic islands from Cape Horn to New Zealand region

species.name: South Polar Skua
species.range: breeds coastal Antarctica, especially Ross Sea; also South Shetland and South Orkney islands (off Antarctic Peninsula); winters to northern offshore waters and North Indian Ocean: mostly clockwise to Japanese and Korean waters and Gulf Stream of eastern USA, then southwestern Canada to northern Baja California and northwestern Africa

species.name: Little Gull
species.range: breeds Baltic region eastward to Sea of Okhotsk and southward to northern Kazakhstan and northeastern China, also rarely Great Lakes, Hudson and James bays (east-central Canada); winters North Atlantic coasts and North, Mediterranean, Baltic, Black, and Caspian seas

species.name: Sabine's Gull
species.range: breeds patchily on Arctic coasts of Greenland, Svalbard, and Siberia eastward to Chukotka Peninsula, St. Lawrence Island, western and northern Alaska, and Arctic Canada; winters coastal and offshore waters of northern South America to northern Chile and western Africa from Angola to southern Africa

species.name: Slender-billed Gull
species.range: breeds patchily on coasts and saline lakes from southern Iberian Peninsula to Central Asia, Pakistan, and coastal far northwestern India, also Mauritania and Senegambia; winters to coasts of Arabian Peninsula and western India

species.name: Black-headed Gull
species.range: breeds southern Greenland, Iceland, and western Europe eastward across Russia to Yakutsk region (eastern Russia), southward through Caspian Seato northeastern China, also west-central Newfoundland (southeastern Canada); winters to Africa, southern Asia, and eastern North America

species.name: Gray-hooded Gull
species.range: marshes, lakes, and coasts of Africa and South America, sub-Saharan Africa (except Congolian forest) and Madagascar; coastal Ecuador and Peru; coastal northeastern Brazil to northeastern Argentina and inland to Salta in the north and La Pampa in the south (north-central Argentina)

species.name: Hartlaub's Gull
species.range: coastal southwestern Namibia to southwestern South Africa

species.name: Franklin's Gull
species.range: breeds prairie marshes of western and northern Alberta eastward to southwestern Manitoba, and southward from east-central Oregon to northwestern Minnesota; winters coasts from Ecuador (including Galapagos) to central Chile

species.name: Pallas's Gull
species.range: breeds patchily on lake islands from Crimea eastward through Kazakhstan and Mongolia to Gansu, Qinghai, and Inner Mongolia (west-central China); winters to coasts, landlocked seas, and rivers from Black Sea eastward across Bay of Bengal to Bangladesh and south-central Myanmar

species.name: Audouin's Gull
species.range: breeds coastal southern Portugal and Spain through Mediterranean and associated seas eastward to Cyprus and southern Türkiye; winters southward to coast of Gambia

species.name: Mediterranean Gull
species.range: breeds inland southern Britain and eastern Spain eastward to southwestern Russia, Ukraine, and Azerbaijan; winters coasts southern Ireland to west-central Africa, Black Sea, and Mediterranean and associated seas

species.name: Sooty Gull
species.range: breeds islands of Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Socotra, southward to northern Kenya and eastward to southern Pakistan; winters to central Tanzania including Zanzibar

species.name: White-eyed Gull
species.range: breeds islands of Red Sea and associated gulfs; winters through Red Sea and nearby coasts

species.name: Common Gull
species.range: breeds mostly wetlands, subarctic and low Arctic of Palearctic from Iceland and northwestern and central Europe to Kamchatka (eastern Siberia), and in the south disjunctly in western and central Asia; winters Europe to northern Africa, Mediterranean, Black and Caspian seas, and Persian Gulf; disjunctly Sea of Okhotsk (southeastern Russia), Japan, and Korean Peninsula to southeastern China

species.name: Caspian Gull
species.range: breeds inland southern Poland and Hungary eastward through Black, Caspian, and Aral seas to eastern Kazakhstan; winters southeastern Europe, Black Sea, eastern Mediterranean, Persian Gulf, and northern Arabian Sea

species.name: Kelp Gull
species.range: breeds coasts and islets of southern continents and islands, mostly in temperate to Antarctic waters, in Africa from Namibia around Cape through northeastern South Africa, and southern Madagascar; in Australia including Tasmania, and New Zealand and associated islands; in South America from northern Peru and southern Brazil south to Tierra del Fuego; and in subantarctic and Antarctic islands; some winter farther north

species.name: Mongolian Gull
species.range: breeds Altai Republic to Lake Baikal (south-central Russia) and Mongolia, Lake Khanka (Heilongjiang, northeastern China), and Yellow Sea islands (western Korean Peninsula); winters mostly to coastal wetlands of Japan, Korean Peninsula, eastern China, and Taiwan

species.name: European Herring Gull
species.range: breeds Iceland, Faroe, and British Isles to Kola Peninsula (northwestern Russia); winters northern and western Europe

species.name: Armenian Gull
species.range: breeds lakes of Caucasus to eastern Türkiye and northwestern Iran; winters to eastern Mediterranean, southern Black and Caspian seas, and Persian Gulf

species.name: Great Black-backed Gull
species.range: breeds North Atlantic coasts, from southern Greenland and Iceland to Svalbard and Baltic states, and coastal and inland northeastern Canada to Great Lakes and Atlantic coast southward to New Jersey; winters to coastal southwestern Europe and coastal Florida

species.name: Lesser Black-backed Gull
species.range: breeds from Greenland, Iceland, and western Europe to central Asia and north-central Siberia; winters mostly coastally to southwestern Europe, Africa (except southwestern and southern), India, and Sri Lanka, and eastern North America

species.name: African Skimmer
species.range: breeds major rivers and lakes of tropical Africa; non-breeders also on coasts

species.name: Brown Noddy
species.range: widespread on tropical and subtropical islands of all oceans; ranges out to sea

species.name: Lesser Noddy
species.range: tropical and subtropical Indian Ocean islands from Seychelles and Mascarenes to Chagos and Maldives (west-central Indian Ocean) and Houtman Abrolhos Islands (west of western Australia) and Ashmore Reef (northwest of Australia; race?); winters to east Africa, Comoros, and northern Madagascar

species.name: Sooty Tern
species.range: widespread in all tropical and subtropical oceans

species.name: Bridled Tern
species.range: widespread tropical and subtropical islands, mostly near continents (except eastern Polynesia and Hawaiian Islands and other remote islands)

species.name: Little Tern
species.range: breeds southwestern Europe and southwestern Russia, central Asia, Mongolia to southeastern Russia, Japan, eastern China, Taiwan and Vietnam; northern and western Africa; Persian Gulf and Iraq to Indus Valley (Pakistan) and Gangetic Plain (north-central India); Sri Lanka; Gulf of Thailand, Malay Peninsula, Singapore, and islands off Greater Sundas; off New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago), Bougainville (northern Solomon Islands); coastal Australia including Tasmania; and Saipan (southern Northern Mariana Islands, northwestern Micronesia); winters in southern portions of range

species.name: Saunders's Tern
species.range: breeds Red Sea and Persian Gulf to islands between India and Sri Lanka; apparently winters mainly Seychelles to Maldives and Cocos (Keeling) Islands

species.name: Damara Tern
species.range: breeds coastal Namibia to Cape Province; winters to northern Angola

species.name: Gull-billed Tern
species.range: local yet widespread inland, rivers and lakes from southwestern Europe to northeastern China; coastal China; coastal western North Atlantic, and Caribbean; coastal southern California and Mexico; coastal South America and inland north-central Argentina; winters to subtropical and tropical coasts (including northern Australia), worldwide (except remote islands)

species.name: Caspian Tern
species.range: breeds patchily coastal Baltic Sea and inland southeast Europe to western Mongolia and Ussuriland (southeastern Russia) and northeastern China and southern Asian coasts; coastal and inland western and southern Africa; Europa (west of southern Madagascar, Mozambique Channel), coastal Madagascar and Aldabra group (southwestern Seychelles); coastal and inland northern and eastern Australia, coastal New Zealand (North, South and Stewart islands); inland Northwest Territories to northeastern Canada, in south to central California and Great Lakes; winters to coastal Africa, Red Sea, Persian Gulf, India, Thailand, Malay Peninsula, and Vietnam; eastern Pacific and Caribbean to Panama

species.name: Whiskered Tern
species.range: widespread in inland marshes of southern, central, and northeastern Eurasia, eastern and southern Africa, and Australia; winters inland Africa, Asia, Australia, and New Guinea

species.name: Black Tern
species.range: breeds inland temperate Canada, USA, and Europe to central Asia; winters coasts and offshore waters, western Africa, and Pacific and Caribbean coastal Mexico to northern South America

species.name: White-winged Tern
species.range: breeds inland south-central and eastern Europe eastward to north-central Siberia and northeastern China; winters Africa eastward to Philippines, Australia (except western deserts and Tasmania), and New Zealand

species.name: Arctic Tern
species.range: breeds circumpolarly, Arctic coasts and inland, from Greenland, Iceland, and British Isles eastward to Kamchatka (eastern Russia), through Aleutian Islands, Alaska mainland through Arctic and subarctic Canada to southeastern Canada; winters subantarctic and Antarctic Ocean to edge of pack-ice

species.name: Antarctic Tern
species.range: widespread in subantarctic and Antarctic islands of South Atlantic, South Indian, western South Pacific, and Antarctic Peninsula; winters north to southern Brazil and southern South Africa

species.name: Common Tern
species.range: widespread, subarctic, temperate, and locally tropical Northern Hemisphere; winters coastally to southern Africa, western Madagascar, southern Australia, and southeastern South America

species.name: White-cheeked Tern
species.range: coastal Kenya to Persian Gulf, Red Sea, and coastal Pakistan

species.name: Black-naped Tern
species.range: islands off tropical Indian and Pacific oceans from Seychelles to Cook Islands (eastern Polynesia)

species.name: Roseate Tern
species.range: patchily temperate to tropical Atlantic, tropical Indian, and subtropical to tropical western Pacific to Vanuatu

species.name: Sandwich Tern
species.range: breeds coastal northwestern to southeastern Europe from British Isles and Baltic Sea to eastern Iberian Peninsula, Mediterranean, Black, and Caspian seas; coastal western North Atlantic from Virginia to Florida, Gulf of Mexico to southern Texas, Campeche Bank (north of Yucatan Peninsula), Belize cays, and West Indies; and islands off Venezuela and the Guianas, coastal eastern Brazil, east-central and southeastern Argentina; winters to coastal southwestern Europe and Mediterranean to Africa, Persian Gulf, India, and Sri Lanka; and to southern Peru and Uruguay

species.name: Lesser Crested Tern
species.range: breeds disjunctly, coasts of south-central Mediterranean, Indian Ocean and marginal seas, and northern Australia; winters to subtropical and tropical Old World waters from northwestern Africa to New Guinea

species.name: West African Crested Tern
species.range: breeds coastal Mauritania to Guinea; winters to Morocco and Namibia

species.name: Great Crested Tern
species.range: coasts of southwestern Africa, North Indian Ocean and marginal seas, through Indonesian and Australian waters from far south Japan to eastern Polynesia

species.name: Greater Flamingo
species.range: southern Europe and Mediterranean basin to southern Africa, Madagascar, and southern Asia

species.name: Lesser Flamingo
species.range: locally from Africa and Madagascar to far northwestern India (mainly Gujarat)

species.name: Little Grebe
species.range: Europe (except north) to central, southern, and eastern Asia and Philippines; Africa and Malagasy region; Java, Sulawesi region, Lesser Sundas, Moluccas, northern New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, and Solomon Islands

species.name: Great Crested Grebe
species.range: breeds temperate Eurasia, locally northwestern India, to northeastern Russia, northeastern China, and north-central Japan; northeastern, eastern, and southern Africa; Australia and South Island (New Zealand); winter withdrawal from northern latitudes

species.name: Eared Grebe
species.range: breeds temperate Eurasia to Russian Far East and northeastern China; eastern and southern Africa; southwestern Canada and western and west-central USA to central Mexico; winters to coasts of northern Africa, Arabian Peninsula, Black and Caspian seas, northwestern Indian subcontinent, southeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan; southern Mexico and east-central USA

species.name: White-tailed Tropicbird
species.range: widespread breeder, all tropical oceans (except eastern Pacific and northeastern Atlantic); pelagic when non-breeding, to waters off eastern Africa, western and southern Sri Lanka, Indonesian Archipelago, and New Guinea waters, east-central Australia, and Gulf Stream north to North Carolina

species.name: Red-billed Tropicbird
species.range: breeds tropical and subtropical islands off northwestern Africa, northern South Atlantic, Persian Gulf region, southeastern Vietnam, northwestern Mexico to Ecuador, and Caribbean; pelagic when non-breeding in tropical and subtropical oceans: in Gulf Stream north to North Carolina, far out to sea in Atlantic, northwestern Indian Ocean to western coast of India, and central California to central Chile

species.name: Red-tailed Tropicbird
species.range: breeds tropical and subtropical islands of South Indian and Pacific oceans; pelagic when not breeding, to waters off southeastern Africa, southwestern and eastern Indonesia, southern Japan, Taiwan, and eastern Australia

species.name: African Penguin
species.range: breeds coastal southern Namibia and southern South Africa; ranges to central Namibia and southeastern Africa

species.name: Snowy Albatross
species.range: breeds high-latitude islands of South Georgia, Prince Edward, Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen, and Macquarie islands; ranges all southern oceans

species.name: Sooty Albatross
species.range: breeds temperate zone islands of South Atlantic and south Indian oceans; ranges through temperate zone of those oceans

species.name: Light-mantled Albatross
species.range: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands; ranges through subantarctic and Antarctic oceans

species.name: Atlantic Yellow-nosed Albatross
species.range: breeds Tristan da Cunha and Gough islands; ranges southern oceans

species.name: Indian Yellow-nosed Albatross
species.range: breeds on southern Indian Ocean islands; ranges mainly southern Indian Ocean between Tropic of Capricorn and Subtropical Convergence

species.name: White-capped Albatross
species.range: breeds Tasmania and Auckland Islands (south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders to southern Indian and Pacific oceans

species.name: Black-browed Albatross
species.range: breeds islands of south Chile, Falkland, South Georgia, and South Sandwich (southeast of South Georgia), Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen (South Indian Ocean), Macquarie (far southeast of Australia), Antipodes, Snares, and Campbell groups (southeast and south of South Island, New Zealand), and Campbell and Jeanette Marie islands (Campbell Islands, south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders are widespread all southern oceans from north of Antarctic Convergence to Tropic of Capricorn

species.name: Wilson's Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds islets in southern Chilean fjords and Cape Horn Archipelago; many islands, coasts, and inland sites in Antarctica; Falklands, South Georgia, Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen (southwestern to southeastern Indian Ocean), and Macquarie islands (far southeast of Australia); non-breeders throughout world oceans except tropical and North Pacific

species.name: White-faced Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds Salvage (northwest of Canary Islands), Canary, and Cape Verde islands (Macaronesia), Tristan da Cunha group including Gough (south-central Atlantic Ocean), southern Australian islets, and New Zealand region; non-breeders range to subtropical waters in North and South Atlantic, northwestern and tropical Indian Ocean to Seychelles, and southeastern Pacific Ocean

species.name: White-bellied Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds tropical and subtropical southern ocean islands: south-central Indian Ocean islands, Lord Howe Island (far east of Australia), Kermadec Islands (northeast of North Island, New Zealand), Rapa (Austral Islands, eastern Polynesia), San Felix and San Ambrosio (Easter Island, southeastern Polynesia), and Juan Fernandez Islands (far west of central Chile); non-breeders range tropical and subtropical southern oceans between Equator and Subtropical Convergence

species.name: Black-bellied Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands of South Georgia, Antarctic Peninsula, Bouvetoya (southwest of Africa), Tristan da Cunha perhaps including Gough Island (south-central Atlantic Ocean); Prince Edward, Crozet, and Kerguelen (southwestern to southeastern Indian Ocean), Bounty, Antipodes, and Auckland islands (southeast and south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders range southern oceans mostly south of Equator to Antarctic Convergence

species.name: European Storm-Petrel
species.range: islets of northeastern North Atlantic from southern Iceland and central Norway to northern Spain, Canary Islands (central Macaronesia), western Africa, and western and north-central Mediterranean Sea

species.name: Leach's Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds northeastern Atlantic from southern Iceland, Faroe Islands, central Norway, Ireland, and Scotland; northwestern Atlantic from southern Labrador to Massachusetts; northwestern Pacific from northeastern Russia and northeastern Japan to Alaska and northern and central Baja California (northwestern Mexico); also off southwestern Africa; non-breeders range to tropical Pacific Ocean mainly north of Tropic of Capricorn, and tropical Atlantic, reaching southern Africa in temperate southeastern Atlantic Ocean

species.name: Swinhoe's Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds mainly islands off Japan, also islets off southeastern Russia, Korean Peninsula, eastern China, and Taiwan; ranges through eastern Indonesian Archipelago to southern India and Sri Lanka, Arabian Sea, and off northeastern African coast; recent records from Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean

species.name: Matsudaira's Storm-Petrel
species.range: breeds Volcano Islands (far southern Japan); disperses westward to Arabian Sea, Seychelles, and off eastern African coast, eastward to western Micronesia, seas of eastern Indonesia, and off northwestern Australia

species.name: Southern Giant-Petrel
species.range: breeds islands and coasts of Antarctica to Heard (Indian Ocean) and Macquarie islands (Australia), and off southern Chile and Argentina; ranges coasts and open water of all southern oceans and cold currents, often south of Antarctic Convergence

species.name: Northern Giant-Petrel
species.range: breeds islands north of Antarctic Convergence from South Georgia to Macquarie (southeast of Australia) and Stewart, Chatham, Antipodes, Auckland, and Campbell islands (New Zealand); ranges coasts and open water of all southern oceans, mostly north of Antarctic Convergence

species.name: Pintado Petrel
species.range: breeds subantarctic and Antarctic islands and coasts; non-breeders range to tropics in cold waters of Benguela Current of southern Africa, southern Australasia, and Humboldt Current of South America north to Ecuador and southern Brazil

species.name: Kerguelen Petrel
species.range: breeds South Georgia, Gough, Inaccessible, Prince Edward, Crozet, and Kerguelen islands; ranges subantarctic and Antarctic waters north of pack-ice

species.name: Great-winged Petrel
species.range: breeds on subtropical to temperate islands from Tristan da Cunha and Gough (south-central South Atlantic Ocean) to Kerguelen Island (southern Indian Ocean), and Eclipse and Coffin islands (off southwestern Australia); non-breeding range in subtropical to temperate South Atlantic and southern Indian oceans from east of southern South America to southern Australian waters

species.name: Soft-plumaged Petrel
species.range: breeds subtropical to subantarctic islands of South Indian and South Atlantic oceans, from Tristan da Cunha and Gough to Maatsuyker (off Tasmania), Macquarie Island (southeast of Australia), and Antipodes Islands (south of New Zealand); ranges to southern waters off Australasia, Africa, and South America

species.name: Atlantic Petrel
species.range: breeds Gough and (at least formerly) Tristan da Cunha; ranges to deep offshore waters of southern Brazil to Argentina, and southwestern Africa

species.name: Broad-billed Prion
species.range: breeds islands off New Zealand and Tristan da Cunha group; disperses southern oceans

species.name: Salvin's Prion
species.range: breeds Prince Edward and Crozet islands; ranges to southern Indian Ocean and southern Australasian seas

species.name: MacGillivray's Prion
species.range: breeds in the southern Atlantic Ocean (Gough Island) and the southern Indian Ocean (off St. Paul Island, formerly also Amsterdam Island); at-sea distribution not well known

species.name: Antarctic Prion
species.range: breeds islets of subantarctic to Antarctic oceans (mainly south of Antarctic Convergence), from Antarctic Peninsula to north of Ross Sea, Macquarie (Australia), and Auckland Islands; ranges from pack-ice to waters off southern South America, Africa, and Australasia

species.name: Slender-billed Prion
species.range: breeds Crozet, Kerguelen, Noir (off southern Chile), and Falkland islands; ranges southern oceans to Humboldt Current of western South America, off coast to southern Brazil, and southern Australasia

species.name: Bulwer's Petrel
species.range: breeds Azores to Cape Verde Islands, Round Island (off Mauritius), Bonin Islands (southern Japan), islands off southern China, Kiribati, Marquesas, Northwestern and main Hawaiian islands, including Johnson Atoll; ranges widely in Atlantic, reaching western Africa, widely in tropical Indian Ocean from Mascarenes eastward to New Guinea and northern Australia, and through tropical Pacific

species.name: Jouanin's Petrel
species.range: breeds Socotra (Yemen) and Halaaniyat islands (Oman); ranges mainly northwestern Indian Ocean, including gulfs of Aden and Oman, off eastern Africa to waters of Seychelles and Mascarenes, eastward to western India and off northwestern Australia

species.name: Mascarene Petrel
species.range: breeds montane Réunion (Mascarenes); formerly also Rodrigues, where extirpated; ranges adjacent Indian Ocean to Seychelles, Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Timor Sea (off western Australia)

species.name: Gray Petrel
species.range: breeds islets of south temperate and subantarctic oceans from Inaccessible and Gough (Atlantic) to Macquarie Island (southeast of Australia), Campbell and Antipodes islands (south of New Zealand); ranges circumpolar subantarctic waters

species.name: White-chinned Petrel
species.range: breeds islets of south temperate and subantarctic oceans north of Antarctic Convergence from Falkland Islands to southern outlying islands of New Zealand; ranges widely in southern oceans, to southern coasts of southern continents and subantarctic islands

species.name: Cory's Shearwater
species.range: eastern Atlantic, breeding from Azores southward to Canary Islands and eastward to Galicia (northwestern Spain) and Berlengas Islands (off west-central Portugal); ranges widely in Atlantic, but mainly in upwelling systems of the Benguela and Agulhas currents

species.name: Flesh-footed Shearwater
species.range: breeds islets off St. Paul (central Indian Ocean), southern Australia, Lord Howe Island (east of Australia), North Island and Cook Strait (New Zealand); ranges to Arabian Sea, eastern Malagasy region, and Sea of Okhotsk to Gulf of Alaska and western USA coast (rare)

species.name: Great Shearwater
species.range: breeds Tristan da Cunha group (mainly) and Kidney Island (Falkland Islands; few); ranges in Atlantic off southern South America and southern Africa, and northward to southern Greenland and northwestern Europe

species.name: Wedge-tailed Shearwater
species.range: widespread in tropical and subtropical Pacific and Indian oceans, breeding on islets from Seychelles and Mascarenes eastward through Ogasawara and Iwo islands (southern Japan) and northern Australia, thence to Hawaii and Revillagigedo Islands (off central Mexico); ranges from northeastern Africa and Malagasy region eastward to southern Baja California and southward to Panama

species.name: Sooty Shearwater
species.range: breeds southeastern Australia (including Macquarie Island), New Zealand including associated subantarctic island groups, far southern South America (including the Falkland Islands), and Tristan da Cunha (south Atlantic Ocean); winters northward in North Atlantic to Greenland and northwestern Europe, and in northern Pacific to Gulf of Alaska and western USA

species.name: Tropical Shearwater
species.range: breeds tropical Indian Ocean in Malagasy region and tropical Pacific Ocean from Vanuatu through Marquesas, and Gambier and Austral islands (eastern Polynesia)

species.name: Persian Shearwater
species.range: breeds Khuriya Muriya Islands (south of Oman), Socotra, and Moheli (=Mwali, Comoros); non-breeders range Arabian Sea to Persian Gulf, Gulf of Aden, Red Sea, Comoros (southwestern Indian Ocean), and western coast of India

species.name: African Openbill
species.range: widespread sub-Saharan Africa in lowland and foothill wetlands, from western Mali and Sierra Leone locally eastward to Sudan, Ethiopia, and western Somalia, southward to northern Namibia and eastern South Africa, and Madagascar; irregular dry season wandering, often northward

species.name: Black Stork
species.range: central and southern Eurasia; southern Africa; winters to central Africa and India

species.name: Abdim's Stork
species.range: sub-Saharan Africa and southwestern Arabia

species.name: African Woolly-necked Stork
species.range: tropical Africa

species.name: White Stork
species.range: lowland to submontane grassland, wetlands, steppe, cultivation, and towns, from continental Europe eastward to Turkestan and far western China, and southward to northwestern Africa and western Iran; western populations winter in Africa (avoiding forest), eastern populations winter in Indian subcontinent

species.name: Saddle-billed Stork
species.range: locally in sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Marabou Stork
species.range: west-central sub-Saharan Africa

species.name: Yellow-billed Stork
species.range: sub-Saharan Africa and Madagascar

species.name: Lesser Frigatebird
